rationale: Closing the recovery scenario's explicit limitation that no snapshot was installed. This successor adds a second test on the same cluster: a member is stopped, another entry is committed, the leader then creates a snapshot at its last index and compacts its log to that index, so the append path can no longer catch up the stopped member and resynchronization must happen through snapshot installation. The member is restarted from its own storage, the clock is advanced so the leader issues heartbeats and then a snapshot, and the harness records whether the snapshot was installed and whether a proposal made afterwards reached the resynchronized member.

experiment.revision_reason: Harness and comparison change: a snapshot-resynchronization test was added to the same harness file, with its own events (snapshot_created, snapshot_installed, snapshot_propose_invocation, snapshot_propose_result) and its own prefix: node 2 is stopped after a committed payload, a second payload is committed, the leader creates a snapshot at its last index from the storage's existing ConfState and compacts its log to that index, node 2 is rebuilt from its own storage, the clock is advanced fifteen rounds with delivery between rounds, and a fresh proposal follows. Three comparisons cover snapshot installation, the proposal returning, and the proposal being applied by the resynchronized member. The append-path recovery test and the other tests in the file are unchanged.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process, with per-node MemoryStorage kept up to date by the driver. After a payload is committed on all nodes, node 2 is stopped and a second payload is committed by nodes 1 and 3. The leader's storage then takes a snapshot at its last index with the storage's ConfState and compacts to that index, so entries the stopped member needs are gone from the append path. Node 2 is rebuilt on its own storage, the clock is advanced fifteen rounds with delivery between rounds, and the harness waits for node 2's applied index to reach the snapshot index and for a fresh proposal to be applied by node 2.
assumptions: The snapshot is produced by the captured MemoryStorage API on the leader, as an application would do when compacting.
The leader only sends a snapshot to a follower it considers recently active, so the clock is advanced after the restart to let heartbeats and responses flow.
The snapshot carries no application state machine data; the observation is the raft-level resynchronization (installation and subsequent participation), not state-machine content.
excluded: Storage loss at the restarted member, multiple restarts, and crash-stop during snapshot installation
ReadOnlyLeaseBased, membership changes and message loss

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3}. Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; propose a payload and wait until all three nodes have applied it. Stop node 2. Propose a second payload and wait until the remaining nodes have applied it. Create a snapshot on node 1's storage at its last index using the storage's ConfState and compact the storage to that index. Rebuild node 2 from its own storage and advance the clock fifteen rounds with delivery between rounds. Wait until node 2's applied index reaches the snapshot index, record the installation, then propose a fresh payload on node 1 and wait until node 2 has applied it.
experiment.responsibility: Resynchronization obligation: a member that cannot be caught up from the log must be restored through a snapshot and must then participate in new decisions again.

comparisons.description: The restarted member installed the snapshot the leader created after compacting past its next index.
A proposal made after the snapshot returned rather than being held or dropped.
The resynchronized member applied that proposal, so it participates in new decisions again.
